issues.description: The problem statement and UML require an addGuestStudents(int) method (single int parameter), and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). However the template defines addGuestStudents with a different signature: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from implementing the expected method signature (and from passing tests that expect the single-parameter version).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification: replace public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). Alternatively, provide an overload public void addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the two-parameter version. Ensure the template and UML/tests use the same single-parameter signature.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem UML and the solution implementation expect addGuestStudents(int). The extra boolean parameter in the template creates a mismatch between the student-facing requirement (and reference solution) and the starter code, which can confuse students about the expected method signature and break automated tests or compile/run expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the UML and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (remove the boolean validateInput parameter) and implement accordingly so students can directly follow the exercise specification.
